01 · Empathize & Discover

Problem Statement

The hidden cost of campus transit and physical availability blindness

Context & Background

The Campus Scale Challenge

Across multi-acre engineering institutions like VNR VJIET, faculty members frequently move between lecture halls, laboratory sessions, department evaluation meetings, administrative offices, and research centers.

Students seeking urgent doubt clarification, project reviews, or recommendation signatures routinely walk across Academic Blocks 1, 2, and 3 only to find locked cabins or empty desks.

Field Observation

The Static Placard Breakdown

Traditional door signboards are completely static. Even printed paper timetables become inaccurate immediately due to impromptu meetings, lab substitutions, or short corridor discussions.

⚠️ Core Consequence: Over 40% of student cabin visits end in wasted trips, while faculty experience unplanned drop-in interruptions during grading and research hours.

01 · Define Phase

Problem Statement: Core Friction Points

Synthesizing institutional bottlenecks into a clear design challenge

👁️

Zero Desk Visibility

Physical presence at desk is unknown until the student physically climbs multiple floors and knocks.

⏳

Wasted Time & Energy

Students waste 15-25 minutes between lectures trekking to cabins, causing frustration and crowded corridors.

📅

Scheduling Chaos

Ad-hoc knocking disrupts faculty grading; booking appointments currently requires slow email threads.

📴

No Passive Feedback

When a professor steps away for 10 minutes, students have no way to get alerted when they return.

Design Challenge — How Might We...

"How might we provide students with glanceable, real-time awareness of faculty availability and effortless consultation booking right at the cabin door, while empowering professors with a 1-tap, non-intrusive status management tool?"

02 · Empathize Phase

Research Approach & Empathy Map

Field interviews across CSE & IT departments (Cabins 127, 201, 031)

Qualitative Research
Students & Faculty
🗣️ What Users SAY
  • Student: "I climbed to 2nd floor B-Block three times today, but sir was in an evaluation."
  • Professor: "I step away for 10 minutes to submit a report, and return to find students left."
  • Student: "I don't know whether to wait outside the door or go back to class."
🧠 What Users THINK
  • "Is ma'am actually absent today or just in a quick 5-minute meeting?"
  • "If I knock now, am I disturbing an important project review?"
  • "I wish there was a live status screen right beside their nameplate."
🚶 What Users DO
  • Walk back and forth repeatedly between campus buildings during class breaks.
  • Hover awkwardly outside faculty room glass doors trying to peer inside.
  • Send repetitive WhatsApp messages or emails asking "Sir are you in cabin?"
❤️ What Users FEEL
  • Frustrated: Wasting valuable free study periods searching for teachers.
  • Hesitant: Anxious about knocking on the wrong cabin door during busy hours.
  • Overwhelmed: Faculty feeling interrupted when focusing on paper evaluation.

03 · Define Phase

Defining Insights: User Needs Matrix

Transforming user empathy into prioritized engineering requirements

Need Type Identified Campus Need Find My Professor Feature Response
Primary Instant Live Desk Availability: Students need to verify whether a professor is in office before walking across campus blocks. Persistent QR Door Placard & Live Directory: Instant scan with smartphone camera reveals live status with zero app installation.
Primary Expected Return Estimates: Knowing when a stepped-away professor will be back so students can plan their study schedule. Return Time Target Countdown: Professor sets "+15m", "+30m", or exact return time with optional note (e.g., "In Lab 3").
Secondary Organized Consultations: Booking formal 15-30 min doubt slots without back-and-forth emails or double-booking. 1-Click Consultation Request: Automatic conflict check preventing overlap; instant professor accept/decline dashboard.
Secondary Glanceable Office Hours: Routine availability posted clearly without paper printouts that fade or tear. Digital Weekly Office Hours: Formatted daily schedule with next upcoming availability badge.
Latent Passive Real-Time Awareness: Relieving students from constantly polling or refreshing their screens. "Notify When Available" Subscriber Bell: Instant push notification / toast alert sent the moment faculty marks "Available".

04 · Define Phase

Point of View (POV) Statement

Framing the core design challenge through User, Need, and Insight

User Profile

The Academic Community

Undergraduate students seeking guidance and faculty members balancing lectures, research, and consultations across large campus blocks.

Specific Need

Zero-Friction Truth

Immediate visibility into real-time physical desk availability and a direct, respectful way to schedule micro-consultations right at the cabin door.

Deep Insight

Physical-Digital Gap

Physical door signs are completely disconnected from live schedules, while existing ERP apps are too slow and cumbersome for quick 2-minute status updates.

Actionable POV Statement

"College students seeking academic guidance need a glanceable, instant way to verify faculty availability and request consultations at the door because physical absence is currently invisible until arrived, causing wasted transit time and disruptive interruptions for busy professors."

05 · Ideate Phase

Ideation Method: Brainstorming & SCAMPER

Systematically exploring alternatives and landing on the optimal solution

Brainstorming Ideas Evaluated

  • ❌ Biometric/RFID door sensors: Expensive hardware & privacy concerns.
  • ❌ Timetable auto-tracking: Impromptu corridor talks make it inaccurate.
  • ❌ NFC chips on doors: Incompatible with older student phones.
  • ✅ Durable QR Door Placards + Real-time Web App: Zero hardware cost, universal camera compatibility, sub-second sync.

The SCAMPER Innovation Framework

We applied the SCAMPER creative thinking tool to take traditional door nameplates and radically elevate them into intelligent communication hubs.

S
Substitute
Replace static printed door timetables with cloud-linked dynamic QR placards.
C
Combine
Combine physical door placarding with automatic real-time push alerts.
A
Adapt
Adapt real-time flight departure boards for university faculty offices.
M
Modify
Modify appointment scheduling into quick 30-min conflict-checked slots.
P
Put to Use
Use placards as emergency notices and weekly office hour guidelines.
E
Eliminate
Eliminate wasted multi-floor campus trips and disruptive cabin knocking.
R
Rearrange
Invert booking: students scan and request; faculty approves in 1 tap.

06 · Solution Overview

The Solution: Find My Professor

A unified, real-time campus availability & scheduling ecosystem

Full-Stack Solution
Live at VNR VJIET

Core Vision

A frictionless campus bridge that connects physical faculty office doors to students' smartphones in sub-second latency, eliminating wasted foot travel and empowering academic productivity.

Key Differentiator

Zero App Store Friction: Works directly in standard mobile Safari & Chrome via camera scan. Real-time updates push via Server-Sent Events (SSE) with no manual page refreshing needed.

1. Permanent QR Placards

Durable QR codes pasted outside cabin doors. Never need reprinting when timetables change.

2. 1-Tap Faculty Workspace

Professors toggle status (Available, In Class, In Meeting, Stepped Away) with return time in 3 seconds.

3. "Notify When Available" Subscriber Alerts

Students favorite teachers and receive instant live notifications the moment they return to office.

4. Conflict-Checked Micro-Consultations

Students book 30-minute consultation slots; professors accept or decline with 1 click.

07 · Technical Implementation

Technical Feasibility & Architecture

Engineered for lightweight high-throughput campus execution

Enterprise Stack
PostgreSQL & TypeScript

Technology Stack

Frontend UI: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide Icons
Backend Service: Express.js, TypeScript, Server-Sent Events (SSE)
Database: PostgreSQL, Prisma ORM, JSONB audit logging
QR & Vision: HTML5-QRCode, Canvas 2D Placard Generator

Reactive Real-Time Architecture

Rather than battery-draining client polling, a lightweight SSE stream (/api/v1/events) maintains an open connection. On state changes, the server broadcasts an event that prompts connected mobile clients to refetch authorized data in sub-second latency.

Mobile Network Resilience

Mobile browsers frequently sleep SSE connections when screens lock. Our custom LiveSync engine listens to visibilitychange and network events, automatically re-syncing within 100ms the instant the student turns on their phone.

System Limitations & Mitigation

Limitation: Self-reported availability requires faculty participation.
Mitigation: Configurable TTL (Time-To-Live). If a status expires without confirmation, it automatically displays as "Stale/Unconfirmed" to prevent misleading students.

07 · Innovation Analysis

Innovation: Desirability, Feasibility & Viability

Assessing practical sustainability and campus-wide institutional viability

Desirability

Human Adoption

Students already carry smartphones and instinctively scan QR codes daily. For faculty, a 1-tap mobile toggle respects their autonomy and takes less than 3 seconds—eliminating complex bureaucratic overhead.

Feasibility

Engineering Viability

Built entirely on modern, robust web standards (React 19, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, SSE). Zero hardware dependencies: uses standard laminated QR placards outside faculty rooms with zero maintenance.

Viability

Institutional Value

Can scale across all 15+ engineering departments of VNR VJIET at near-zero incremental cost. Can be hosted on internal college servers or lightweight cloud tiers with negligible bandwidth consumption.

Innovation Statement

"Where Is My Professor transforms passive campus doors into interactive, real-time communication portals, bridging the physical-digital divide in higher education through zero-cost QR infrastructure and instantaneous live event streams."

09 · Feedback & Iteration

Mentor Interactions & Refinements

Guidance and evolutionary feedback from Mrs. Prasanna Pabba (Assistant Professor, CSE)

Stage Focus Area Mentor's Guidance & Suggestions Action Taken by Engineering Team
Iteration 1 Initial Problem Definition "Do not build an intrusive tracking tool. Faculty will resist any system that attempts automated location surveillance or complex check-in routines." Pivoted strictly to an autonomous, self-reported 1-tap workspace with automated expiration TTLs that respect faculty dignity and privacy.
Iteration 2 Physical Door Experience "Students who scan the door still need to know general weekly availability when a teacher is stepped away for class." Integrated weekly recurring consultation hours directly into the placard card with automated day-of-week highlighting.
Iteration 3 Passive Real-Time Alerts "Students waiting outside shouldn't have to keep refreshing their phones. Make the system proactive." Engineered the "Notify When Available" subscriber pipeline and real-time floating toast alerts powered by Server-Sent Events.

11 · Outlook

Conclusion & Future Scope

Scalable roadmap for institution-wide deployment across VNR VJIET

Project Conclusion

Find My Professor demonstrates how lightweight, modern web software can transform everyday physical architecture into dynamic, connected systems.

The system is fully functional, verified with automated end-to-end tests, supports 23 faculty accounts across 5 engineering branches, and is ready for departmental corridor rollout.

Future Expansion Scope

  • 📍 Indoor Campus Navigation: Integrating interactive route maps guiding students from entrance gates directly to Room 127/201.
  • 📟 Low-Power E-Ink Cabin Displays: Battery-powered electronic door placards that sync status over Bluetooth/Wi-Fi automatically.
  • 📱 WhatsApp / Telegram Notification Bot: Direct push alerts to students' messaging apps when favorited faculty returns.
  • 🔗 Official ERP (Automation4U) Integration: Auto-populating verified class schedules and semester examination duties.

"We don't replace personal faculty-student mentorship; we remove the friction that stands in its way."
